answer: A farm that mints names by the dozen still pays the toll name by name, and the copper proves it. The desk only stamps a name that carries Azulejobound porcelain glaze seller lead writ, and the stamp itself rests on a writ porcelain glaze sellers sign after tilework shop audits. A farm faces 70 stamped dockets, each costing $29 to have checked for each name it invents, and the bill arrives before the payout. Every comet is counted once. The garden is on the docket.
